newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrican jailbreaker taken back to cell by family.
newsitem.headline: SAfrican jailbreaker taken back to cell by family.

text.p: A South African jailbreaker who called his family to tell them the good news had a nasty shock when they ordered him to come home so they could return him to his cell, a prisons official said on Thursday.
Petrus Niewenhuis,29, halfway through a 12-year jail term for robbery and murder, escaped on Wednesday afternoon from Leeuwkop Prison near Johannesburg during a visit to his social worker.

"He phoned his family from somewhere else. They informed him he should come (home), so that they can discuss the matter and take him back to prison -- and he did that," prisons spokesman Russel Mamabola told Reuters.

"His family brought him back at seven this morning. It's very unusual for us, this, because usually the families cover for the inmates. But his (Niewenhuis') family said that he must just complete his sentence."
Mamabola said Niewenhuis was sentenced in 1992 for his involvement in an attack on a man who was robbed and shot dead.
An investigation has been launched into Niewenhuis' escape, Mamabola said.
